svg.title: The high-pressure alarm is sounding on a ventilated client. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: A high-pressure alarm means resistance, so the nurse assesses the client first and then works the fixable causes: secretions, kinks or water in the tubing, biting, and bronchospasm. Silencing the alarm without assessing and disconnecting the client from support are both unsafe.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Ventilator Alarms
Read the situation
The high-pressure alarm is sounding on a
ventilated client. Which nursing actions
are appropriate? Select all that apply.
What fits here
Check the tubing for kinks or accumulated
water · Suction the airway if secretions
are present · Assess the client's airway,
chest rise, and color · Insert a bite
block if the client is…
Why it fits
A high-pressure alarm means resistance, so
the nurse assesses the client first and
then works the fixable causes: secretions,
kinks or water in the tubing, biting, and
bronchospasm. Silencing the alarm without
assessing and disconnecting the client
from support are both unsafe.
